newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks power to new highs on U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks power to new highs on U.S. gains.

text.p: Norwegian shares steamed to new record highs on Tuesday fuelled by a strong Wall Street, a firmer dollar and higher oil prices.
Brokers said interest had moved from the cyclical shares to industrial stocks.
Oslo's Total share index closed at an all-time high at 884.73 points, a gain of 0.8 percent from Monday. Turnover was a healthy 831 million crowns, up 45 percent from a day earlier.
"Sentiment is very positive. We are climbing on the back of Wall Street, but also people generally don't want to sell," said one broker.
"Many investors sold in September when they expected the market to fall so they're now holding on."

Food and beverage conglomerate Orkla jumped more than two percent, or 8.50 crowns, to 400.50 crowns. Dealers said the rise reflected a recovery from a dip a week ago and foreign interest in the company. "There's someone who wants to buy and that's the price the sellers want. It back to where it was last week," said one dealer.
Saga Petroleum also gained as oil prices hit $25 per barrel and also on reports that the company was considering a buy out of British group Santa Fe Exploration.
